title: Dependency liveness map and cutover orchestration playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create an operational playbook and lightweight data model that makes cross-team roadmap dependencies observable as a "liveness" signal, ties those signals to automated cutover choreography, and provides clear guardrails for last-mile escalation. The goal is to reduce scope slippage caused by hidden downstream blockers during major rollout windows (runtime, console, Dedicated).
goals: Define a dependency liveness schema that teams can populate (readiness, test-coverage, infra-provision, security-review)
Produce a visual 'liveness map' for every major initiative that shows per-team readiness and critical path items
Ship an orchestration playbook and templated automation hooks for canary/cutover that integrates with alerts and incident channels
success_metrics: % of release lanes with a liveness map before the start of the freeze window >= 90%
Reduction in cross-team blocker-driven rollbacks by 40% vs previous quarter
Mean time to identify owner for a blocking dependency <= 2 hours during cutover

acceptance_criteria: Teams can annotate dependencies with the liveness schema fields via a lightweight form or CSV import
Console shows a per-initiative liveness map and highlights critical-path items
Escalation flow triggers a named on-call and creates a short-lived 'escalation issue' in Linear when readiness falls below thresholds
Playbook includes decision trees for rollback vs mitigation with explicit owner handoff steps
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Pilot): 2 initiatives (runtime-1.21 rollout + console-2026.03) with Eng/Design/Security/Infra participates
Phase 2: Open template to all PMs and require liveness map for any release > P1 impact
Phase 3: Automate import from CI runs and security scan outputs to update liveness fields
automation_hooks: Slack channel integration: warn when readiness drops below 75% for a lane
PagerDuty escalation: fire after 2 unanswered Slack pings on critical-path items
Linear issue automation: create PM-owned 'escalation' issue tagged with the initiative when a dependency enters blocked state
open_questions: Which teams will be required to keep liveness fields updated vs optional?
What is the preservation policy for liveness history across quarters?
Do we derive readiness from objective signals (CI green, infra provisioned) or rely on manual attestation?
decisions: Use a hybrid model: basic readiness fields are required; signal auto-fill from CI/security is optional but recommended
Escalation window set to 48 hours pre-cutover for non-critical items; 72 hours for infra/security blockers
Visual liveness map will be read-only for pilot; editing through a small form to avoid accidental drift
